analysis.evidence: The suffix ךָ identifies whom God will make into a nation, and לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל specifies the promised result, “into a great nation.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes a Qal imperfect, first person common singular. The object suffix ךָ is second person masculine singular and refers to Abram.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל, “I will make you into a great nation,” גּוֹי names the people God promises will come from Abram.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לְ marks the result of וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ, “I will make you.” The noun is masculine singular absolute, and the adjective גָּדוֹל agrees with it.
analysis.sense: a people counted as a nation

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל, “I will make you a great nation,” גָּדוֹל modifies גוֹי and describes the promised nation as numerous.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective agreeing with גוֹי.

analysis.evidence: God addresses Abram in the first person. The promises on either side, “I will make you a great nation” and “I will make your name great,” show what this blessing will mean for him.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ joins a first-person common singular Piel imperfect to the preceding promise. The second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ is the direct object and refers to Abram.
analysis.sense: to confer divine blessing on a person

analysis.evidence: The speaker promises to bless Abram and then takes שְׁמֶךָ, “your name,” as the object of וַאֲגַדְּלָה. The promise is “and I will make your name great.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ precedes a Piel first-person common singular cohortative. The אֲ־ prefix marks the speaker, and the ־ָה ending marks the cohortative.
analysis.sense: make great (a man, a name, a throne)

draft.change: Add Genesis 12:2 as evidence for the existing renown sense of שֵׁם.
draft.definition: A person’s name as their reputation among others.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:2 expresses the promise of renown by saying that Yahweh will make Abram’s name great.

analysis.evidence: In וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ, “I will make your name great,” Abram’s name is the object of the promise. Its greatness describes the renown Abram will gain.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a second-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: After God tells Abram וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ, “I will bless you,” the imperative הְיֵה takes בְּרָכָה, “a blessing,” as its predicate. God calls on Abram to be a blessing.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וֶ joins the preceding promise to a Qal imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram.

analysis.evidence: In וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה, “and be a blessing,” the imperative וֶהְיֵה addresses Abram. The noun is its predicate and describes what Abram is to be.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix. The initial ב is part of the noun.
analysis.sense: a person in whom blessing is seen
